aiOverview.content: The U.S. Virgin Islands (USVI), a stunning Caribbean territory including St. Thomas, St. John, and St. Croix, offer pristine white-sand beaches like Trunk Bay, snorkeling, and historic sites. Visitors can enjoy hiking in Virgin Islands National Park, sailing, and diving while staying in luxurious resorts or local villas. Top Attractions & Things to Do Beaches: Trunk Bay (St. John), Magens Bay (St. Thomas), and Buck Island Reef National Monument (St. Croix) are top-rated. Activities: Snorkeling and diving (especially at Water Lemon Cay), hiking the Reef Bay Trail, and exploring the Annaberg Sugar Plantation ruins. Culture & Shopping: Shopping in Charlotte Amalie (the capital) and visiting historic sites like Fort Christian. Boating: Sailing, yachting, and taking day trips to neighboring islands. Key Islands (USVI) St. Thomas: Known for its bustling capital, Charlotte Amalie, duty-free shopping, and harbor. St. John: Quiet, relaxing, with over half the island protected as a National Park. St. Croix: The largest island, known for its historic towns of Christiansted and Frederiksted, and agricultural history. Water Island: The smallest, offering a secluded getaway. Where to Stay Resorts/Hotels: Ranging from luxury beachfront resorts to charming boutique hotels, primarily in St. Thomas and St. Croix. Villas & Rentals: Very popular on St. John and St. Thomas for a more private experience. Camping: Available in dedicated areas of St. John. Essential Information Population: Approximately 87,000 [approximate, based on typical USVI population data]. Weather: Tropical year-round, averaging 77∘F77 raised to the composed with power F77∘F in winter to 82∘F82 raised to the composed with power F82∘F in summer, with the highest rainfall from June to November. Entry: As a U.S. Territory, U.S. citizens can visit without a passport, while others need a passport. Best Time to Visit: December to April for the best weather, though prices are higher. Getting Around: Driving is on the left side of the road, and renting a jeep is popular, particularly on St. John.
